collection: TOEFL iBT 2026 original campus announcement practice
note: Six original announcements of 40–85 words. Two practice questions per announcement are an author choice; the retrieved overview does not establish a fixed question count. Requires supervised live delivery. Keep scripts, answers and explanations out of learner view.
examinerInstructions: Read each announcement at a natural pace, then present its two questions and four written choices per question. Award one classroom practice point per correct answer. These points have no TOEFL scale conversion.

listeningSets.title: Room change
listeningSets.examinerScript: Attention, first-year design students. This afternoon’s materials demonstration will take place in Studio Three instead of the main workshop because the workshop extraction system is being serviced. The starting time is unchanged. Please bring your sketchbooks, but leave your project models in the usual storage area. Staff will demonstrate the materials, so you will not need your own tools for this session.

listeningSets.title: Submission check
listeningSets.examinerScript: Before you leave today, please check the file you uploaded for the history assignment. Several students have submitted a document that opens to a blank page. If yours has that problem, upload a working copy by tomorrow morning and send me a brief message. If your file displays correctly, you do not need to submit it again. This check concerns file access, not changes to your argument.

listeningSets.title: Volunteer briefing
listeningSets.examinerScript: Welcome to the campus book drive. Today we are sorting donations by intended age group, rather than by subject. Put books for younger readers on the tables near the windows and books for adults along the opposite wall. If you cannot decide where a book belongs, place it in the tray beside my desk. We will review those uncertain items together after the first sorting round.

listeningSets.title: Presentation support
listeningSets.examinerScript: The language centre is offering short practice sessions for students preparing conference presentations. These sessions focus on explaining ideas clearly to listeners outside your field. They are not proofreading appointments, so bring an outline and be ready to speak for three minutes. A partner will then explain what they understood. You can use that feedback to decide which terms or examples need more explanation.

listeningSets.title: Bicycle access
listeningSets.examinerScript: From Monday, bicycles must be walked through the central courtyard between classes. The route will remain open, but it becomes crowded when lectures finish. Riders may use the outer path if they prefer to stay on their bicycles. Signs will mark both routes. This change follows several near misses, and we will review how well it works after two weeks.

listeningSets.title: Exhibition recordings
listeningSets.examinerScript: The student exhibition opens this evening. Visitors may photograph the displays, but please ask the presenter before recording any explanation. Some projects contain interviews whose participants agreed to exhibition use only. The printed summaries can be taken away, and additional copies are available at reception. If you plan to write about a project, the presenter can help you find material that is suitable to quote.

questions.subject: Listening
questions.learningObjective: Identify the purpose, important details, conditions or likely actions in a short campus announcement.
questions.prompt: What is the main purpose of the message to design students?
options: To announce a change of room for a demonstration.
To cancel a materials demonstration.
To ask students to repair workshop equipment.
To introduce a new design course.
questions.answer: To announce a change of room for a demonstration.
questions.explanation: The message relocates the demonstration while keeping the starting time.

questions.subject: Listening
questions.learningObjective: Identify the purpose, important details, conditions or likely actions in a short campus announcement.
questions.prompt: What should the design students bring to the session?
options: Their project models.
Their personal tool sets.
Their sketchbooks.
Their storage keys.
questions.explanation: Students are told to bring sketchbooks and leave models in storage.

questions.subject: Listening
questions.learningObjective: Identify the purpose, important details, conditions or likely actions in a short campus announcement.
questions.prompt: Why are history students asked to check their uploaded files?
options: The essay topic has changed.
Some documents cannot be read properly.
The assignment deadline has been cancelled.
All students must rewrite their arguments.
questions.answer: Some documents cannot be read properly.
questions.explanation: Some uploaded documents display a blank page.

questions.subject: Listening
questions.learningObjective: Identify the purpose, important details, conditions or likely actions in a short campus announcement.
questions.prompt: What should a student do if the uploaded history file displays correctly?
options: Upload it to a different course.
Send a new argument to the teacher.
Delete the original file immediately.
Leave the submission as it is.
questions.answer: Leave the submission as it is.
questions.explanation: The speaker says a correctly displayed file does not need resubmission.

questions.subject: Listening
questions.learningObjective: Identify the purpose, important details, conditions or likely actions in a short campus announcement.
questions.prompt: How should volunteers organise books during the first sorting round?
options: By the authors’ surnames.
By the dates of publication.
By the intended readers’ age groups.
By the subjects on their covers.
questions.answer: By the intended readers’ age groups.
questions.explanation: The speaker specifies age group rather than subject.

questions.subject: Listening
questions.learningObjective: Identify the purpose, important details, conditions or likely actions in a short campus announcement.
questions.prompt: Where should a volunteer put a book that is difficult to classify?
options: In the tray beside the organiser’s desk.
Back into a sealed donation box.
On the tables near the windows.
Along the wall with the adult books.
questions.answer: In the tray beside the organiser’s desk.
questions.explanation: Uncertain items go in the tray for later joint review.

questions.subject: Listening
questions.learningObjective: Identify the purpose, important details, conditions or likely actions in a short campus announcement.
questions.prompt: What will participants mainly practise at the language-centre sessions?
options: Correcting spelling in finished articles.
Designing posters for a student event.
Memorising a full conference speech.
Making specialist ideas clear to other listeners.
questions.answer: Making specialist ideas clear to other listeners.
questions.explanation: The sessions target clear explanation to people outside the speaker’s field.

questions.subject: Listening
questions.learningObjective: Identify the purpose, important details, conditions or likely actions in a short campus announcement.
questions.prompt: Why will a partner explain what they understood from the practice presentation?
options: To choose the next conference venue.
To help the speaker identify unclear parts.
To replace the speaker at the conference.
To assess the spelling of the outline.
questions.answer: To help the speaker identify unclear parts.
questions.explanation: The partner’s response reveals terms or examples that require more explanation.

questions.subject: Listening
questions.learningObjective: Identify the purpose, important details, conditions or likely actions in a short campus announcement.
questions.prompt: What is changing for cyclists in the central courtyard?
options: They must register their bicycles each day.
They may ride there only after dark.
They must walk their bicycles between classes.
They must avoid the courtyard for the entire term.
questions.answer: They must walk their bicycles between classes.
questions.explanation: The message requires cyclists to walk through the courtyard between classes.

questions.subject: Listening
questions.learningObjective: Identify the purpose, important details, conditions or likely actions in a short campus announcement.
questions.prompt: What can a cyclist do to continue riding between classes?
options: Use the outer path.
Wait inside a lecture room.
Remove the bicycle’s lights.
Cross the crowded courtyard faster.
questions.explanation: The outer path is offered to those who want to remain on their bicycles.

questions.subject: Listening
questions.learningObjective: Identify the purpose, important details, conditions or likely actions in a short campus announcement.
questions.prompt: What should a visitor do before recording a presenter’s explanation?
options: Collect every printed summary.
Ask the presenter for permission.
Register for a new interview project.
Wait until the exhibition has closed.
questions.explanation: Visitors are explicitly asked to seek permission before recording explanations.

questions.subject: Listening
questions.learningObjective: Identify the purpose, important details, conditions or likely actions in a short campus announcement.
questions.prompt: Why may some exhibition material be unsuitable for wider recording?
options: The exhibition has no printed summaries.
The projects have not been completed.
All photography of displays is forbidden.
Some interview permissions cover exhibition use only.
questions.answer: Some interview permissions cover exhibition use only.
questions.explanation: The restriction reflects the limited uses agreed by interview participants.
